Platts Heath Primary School
A small village primary school near Lenham in Kent
We are a small village primary school, located in the picturesque hamlet of Platts Heath, near Lenham, in the middle of Kent.
As part of the ASPIRE Federation, we aim to be an outstanding school at the heart of our culturally diverse communities. We strive for excellence, enabling our children to achieve their highest potential in all areas of the curriculum.
We are passionate about our school and about bringing out the best in the pupils as well as the staff.
We have a dedicated team of teachers and support staff who provide the children with as many opportunities as possible to learn in a fun and exciting way. Our pupils are equipped with the skills they need to make good progress through their primary education so they can confidently make the transition to secondary school.
If you would like to visit our school please get in touch with Mrs Branchett in the School Office.

pageCache.text:
A small village primary school near Lenham in Kent
Pupils in years R, 1 and 2 are eligible for free universal school meals*.
Children in years 3-6 are required to pay for school meals and currently cost £2.70 per meal.
Meals need to be paid for in advance via the online portal. Click here for access.
If families are on low income or in receipt of certain benefits can apply for Free School Meals via the KCC website. To check if you are eligible for these, click the link below;
* Please apply if your child is in year R, 1 or 2, as this will result in additional funding being available in school to support your child with other activities.
School meals are provided by Caterlink, an external catering contractor and are freshly prepared daily. The current menu is available on this page to download.
If your child has any food allergies, you must complete and return the listed form to enable the catering company to prepare a bespoke menu. These forms are availble on request.

ASPIRE Federation is a caring and supporting environment with career opportunities for new and existing staff.
We are always pleased to receive CVs and other details from people interested in working with us.
So, if you share our passion for nurturing curiosity and creativity through an inspiring, broad and engaging curriculum, where learning is at the heart of all that we do, and would be interested in working for us, visit our careers website.
For any enquiries regarding our vacancies, please get in touch with us.

We know that wearing a uniform is a badge of pride, creates an identity for a school and is an important part of being a school pupil. It teaches children to dress smartly and take pride in their appearance. That’s why we have developed a smart and comfortable uniform which is liked by both our children and their parents. Successes have included school fairs, discos, raffles, afternoon tea/coffee-get-togethers and delicious cake sales. Find out more about PTA

pageCache.pageTitle: Emergency closures » Platts Heath Primary School
pageCache.text:
A small village primary school near Lenham in Kent
If for any reason the school needs to close due to an emergency, parents will be contacted via our email and mobile text service.
When children start school these contact details will be requested and added to our system. If they change at any time, please notify us immediately so we can always contact you as necessary.
Bad weather
In the case of bad weather we shall try and keep the school open as much as possible.
However, if we are unable to do so and have to close the school, we shall notify you via the Kent Closures website.
If you sign up to this website you will receive a notification if our school is closed. You can also listen to local radio stations who will also be updated with current closure information.

A small village primary school near Lenham in Kent
Parent View is an online questionnaire that allows parents and carers to give their views about our school directly to Ofsted.
What is Parent View?
Parent View gives you the chance to tell Ofsted what you think about our, from the quality of teaching to dealing with bullying and poor behaviour.
The survey can be completed at any time; you don’t have to wait until our school is being inspected.
Ofsted will use the information you provide when making decisions about which schools to inspect and when.
It is also the main mechanism for parents to give their views about their child’s school to inspectors at the time of a school inspection.
You can also view the results from other parents during previous years.

A small village primary school near Lenham in Kent
Our PTFA (Parents, Teachers and Friends Association) is our parent and staff group.
They raise funds, organise events and trips and support the school in a variety of ways. Successes have included school fairs, discos, raffles, afternoon tea/coffee-get-togethers and delicious cake sales.
The PTFA is a friendly group of people who want to support the school by providing “extras”, mainly through fundraising activities.
Meetings are informal and everyone is welcome – it’s a great way to meet other parents while doing something that really benefits all of our children.
In a time when school budgets continue to shrink, the work of the PTFA is more important than ever.
If you’d like to join us (there is no need to attend every meeting – we know that you all have busy lives) please leave a message in the office and we promise to get back to you. If you can’t come along to meetings but might be able to help at events, please let us know.
We really are a friendly bunch!

pageCache.pageTitle: School day » Platts Heath Primary School
pageCache.text:
A small village primary school near Lenham in Kent
Our school days are designed to help our children develop their knowledge and confidence to enable them to achieve their highest potential in all areas of the curriculum.
The school gates open at 8:30am when your child will be welcomed to start their school day.
For the safety of all our children, please use the School Lane entrance.
Any child arriving after registration at 8.45am will need to enter via the school office.
All children enjoy a 15 minute break time from 10.15am
Lunchtime runs from 12pm – 1pm
An afternoon break is arranged on a daily basis depending on PE and weather conditions.
Our school day finishes at:
The gates open at 3.10pm and parents are encouraged to enter the playground to collect their child/ren
Total time in school 6 hours and 45 minutes per day
Total time per week is 33 hours and 45 minutes
ASPIRE WAC Provision
Letters will be sent out by end of week 1 of every term to enroll in after school clubs

As a school, we are part of the Government initiative providing milk for children
This service is provided by a company called Cool Milk, who process the orders, liaise with our local dairy and ensure our milk is delivered on time.
If your child is over 5 years of age and does not receive milk at school and you would like them to, you can register your child online.
Children under 5 will receive free milk and this is organised by the school – parents do not need to take any action.
Children in receipt of Free School Meals are also entitled to free milk. If you think your child is eligible and you would like them to have milk please contact the school office
If you require further information please contact Cool Milk on 0333 400 1199 or click the link to the website below

pageCache.pageTitle: School uniform » Platts Heath Primary School
pageCache.text:
A small village primary school near Lenham in Kent
We know that wearing a uniform is a badge of pride, creates an identity for a school and is an important part of being a school pupil. It teaches children to dress smartly and take pride in their appearance.
That’s why we have developed a smart and comfortable uniform which is liked by both our children and their parents.
Our school uniform
Our school has an active uniform. Full guidance details are below:
ASPIRE Uniform Policy
Active uniform pupils are asked to wear as follows:
All children will be required to wear our Active Uniform on PE days. If your child is new to the school we understand it may take time for your branded items to arrive and unbranded jumpers/hoodies are acceptable. We sell pre-loved uniform regularly after school – look out for details in our newsletters.
To ensure the smooth running of our classes and to cause the least amount of stress (to all), we ask you to ensure that all your child’s items of clothing are labelled clearly with their name.
The wearing of jewellery to school is not allowed and children are asked to only wear stud earrings (one in each ear) if they have their ears pierced. These should not be fashion earrings but plain gold/silver studs please. These will have to be removed by your child for PE and swimming.
A small functional watch may be worn.
Purple hoodie/zip up top
White t-shirt
Black tracksuit bottoms/sports leggings/skort or shorts

Purple sweatshirt/cardigan

pageCache.pageTitle: Special Educational Needs and Disability » Platts Heath Primary School
pageCache.text:
A small village primary school near Lenham in Kent
Our staff work hard in identifying any special educational needs (SEN) that pupils may have to ensure that they can access the curriculum being taught and successfully progress.
Everyone in the school community, governors, staff, pupils and parents have a positive part to play in achieving provision for pupils with SEN.
If you have any concerns with your child’s learning please speak to their class teacher in the first instance.
Where necessary, they will consult with the school Senco and they will work together with you to put strategies in place to support your child.
Our Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (Senco)
Mrs Emma Le-Mar is the Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (Senco) for the ASPIRE Federation and is responsible for the day to day operation of the SEN policy.
Definition of Special Educational Needs (SEN)
A child or young person has SEN if they have a learning difficulty or disability which calls for special educational provision to be made for him or her.
A child of compulsory school age or a young person has a learning difficulty if he or she:
a) Has a significantly greater difficulty in learning than the majority of others of the same age, or
b) Has a disability which prevents or hinders him or her from making use offacilities of a kind generally provided for others of the same age inmainstream schools or mainstream post-16 institutions
[SEND Code of Practice, 2015]
